model_annotation: The plot titled “ViT, ImageNet1k” illustrates how “Sharpness composition” varies over training for three separate components shown as distinct lines. The x-axis is labeled “Training Steps,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0 to about 37,700 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0, 7,540, 15,080, 22,620, 30,160, and 37,700. The y-axis is labeled “Sharpness composition” and is drawn on a signed logarithmic-style scale with a marked zero baseline and tick labels at approximately \(10^{0}\) and \(10^{-1}\) above zero and \(-10^{-1}\) and \(-10^{0}\) below zero. A solid blue line (no markers) begins near 0 at step 0, rises steeply within the earliest portion of training to around the \(10^{0}\) level (near 1), and then stays close to that level for most steps with small fluctuations, ending slightly below 1 (around 0.8–0.9) near 37,700. A solid orange line (no markers) starts near \(10^{0}\) (about 1) at step 0, dips early to roughly 0.6–0.7, then gradually increases across training, approaching around 0.85–0.95 by the final steps. A solid light-brown/gray line (no markers) starts near 0 at step 0, drops quickly into negative values past \(-10^{-1}\), reaches near \(-10^{0}\) (around -0.8 to -0.9) within the early part of training, and then remains near that negative range with minor variation, trending slightly upward (less negative) toward roughly -0.7 to -0.8 by about 37,700 steps.
